taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: an erect shrub, 1-3 m. high, or in forests becoming a vine; the shrub is drawn.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: an erect shrub, 1-3 m. high; as a vine climbing trees to 40 m., which is not drawn.

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Toxicodendron diversilobum: a many-stemmed, deciduous, native shrub or woody vine.

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Toxicodendron diversilobum: a shrub or woody vine.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: leaves 3-foliolate, deciduous.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Leaves borne singly, alternate along the stems, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 268681104, 56703050, 276456081, 119554185, 121053471, 159668842, 6395203, 74688895): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: leaves 3-foliolate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: leaves 3-foliolate, the lateral leaflets usually sessile and the terminal one stalked, as in a pinnate leaf.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: leaflets lobed or toothed but not divided again.

traits.leaflets.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: leaves 3-foliolate; FEIS: three (sometimes five) leaflets.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: the lateral leaflets usually sessile, the terminal one stalked.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 6 cm to 15 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaflets 2.5 cm to 7 cm long, the terminal one the largest, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 5 cm to 12 cm across their lateral leaflets, as in the photos.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 2 cm to 6 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: leaflets ovate, obovate or elliptical.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: obtuse or rounded at the apex.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: variously lobed or toothed, or rarely entire; FEIS: usually resembling oak leaves.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: panicles axillary, loosely flowered.

traits.flowering_position.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: panicles axillary; FEIS: small flowers occur in leaf axils.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 50, Rhus diversiloba: panicles drooping or spreading.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: panicles 3 cm to 8 cm long.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: 4 to 8 side branches to a panicle, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 268681104, 56703050, 276456081, 119554185, 121053471, 159668842, 6395203, 74688895): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 15 to 40 flowers in a panicle, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 268681104, 56703050, 276456081, 119554185, 121053471, 159668842, 6395203, 74688895): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: flowers 4 mm to 6 mm across.

traits.flower_colour.note: Petals greenish cream; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 268681104, 56703050, 276456081, 119554185, 121053471, 159668842, 6395203, 74688895): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS species review, Toxicodendron diversilobum: male and female flowers on separate plants.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus diversiloba: drupes glabrous, with a thin deciduous epicarp and a waxy-persistent mesocarp.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus diversiloba: drupes 4-6 mm. in diameter.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: FEIS species review, Toxicodendron diversilobum: the fruits are white drupes; sRGB by eye.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus diversiloba: flowering April and May.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: drupes ripe July to September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a dense many-stemmed shrub of glossy, lobed leaves in threes, the loose cream flower panicles hanging from the leaf axils.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Pacific poison oak from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.8 m tall at 12 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion, phase C batch 3 (2026-10-18): sizes and forms from Abrams, FEIS and Dendrology, counts from photos.
